title: Toolcall selection and argument-conformance regression harness (CI-gated, config-aware)
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Build a config-aware evaluation harness that continuously measures two complementary signals for function/tool calling: (1) tool selection accuracy (does the model choose the correct tool for a given prompt) and (2) argument-conformance (do the returned arguments match the tool's schema/validation rules). The harness must: run as a CI job on PRs that touch model artifacts or runtime config, run nightly on our canary and baseline model fleet, and be able to re-score historical runs when kernel/quantization/config changes are deployed. Outputs should feed a scoreboard and automated regression alerts that can gate canary rollouts.

Key design considerations: integrate with existing invocation test corpus (mix of synthetic edge cases + anonymized production prompts), preserve PII by using hashed/blocked samples for production traces, measure per-config and per-model deltas, support sampling throttles to control compute cost, and provide lineage metadata (model version, runtime config hash, Docker image, GPU type) for each run. The harness will emit metrics to our observability pipeline (selection_accuracy, arg_precision, arg_recall, arg_f1, schema_violation_rate) and attach a sample of failing invocations for triage.

We must decide how to handle ambiguous ground truth for tool selection (multiple acceptable tools) — proposed approach: label primary/secondary tool choices in dataset and compute top-1 / top-3 accuracy with weighted scoring. For argument conformance, use a layered validator: JSON Schema + runtime semantic checks (e.g., numeric ranges, timestamp formats, idempotency tokens). The system will produce a lightweight HTML report and a canonical machine-readable artifacts bundle (CSV + JSONL) for offline analysis and reproducibility.

Integration points: GitHub Actions for PR gating (runs fast subset), Airflow nightly DAG for full sweep, Redwood Console dashboard for trend visualizations, PagerDuty/Slack for high-severity regressions (automated when selection_accuracy drops >3% absolute or arg_f1 < 0.85 for two consecutive runs).

Links: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INVOK/Toolcall+Conformance+Harness, proto dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/invocation/arg-conformance, seed corpus: gs://redwood-evals/toolcall-corpus/v1/, initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4762
acceptance_criteria: CI PR check runs a fast subset and fails the PR if selection_accuracy drops >4% relative to baseline for the touched model
Nightly full sweep computes per-model and per-config deltas and writes results to evals-snapshot bucket
Automated alerts created when any model+config combo triggers defined thresholds; Slack channel receives triage bundle with sample failures
HTML human-readable report and machine-readable artifacts attach to the run in the Dashboard and to the GitHub PR
Support for versioned config hash and rollback scoring so we can compare pre/post kernel/quantization changes
tasks: Design data schema for eval outputs (metrics + failure samples) and publish in repo (ENG spec)
Implement fast PR subset runner in GitHub Actions using 50 prioritized test cases
Build batch runner in Airflow that accepts model+config matrix and schedules per-cluster runs
Implement argument validator library (JSON Schema + semantic hooks) and integrate with runtime SDK
Wire metric emission into observability (Prometheus+Traces) and create Dashboard panels
Add regression gating rules to canary rollout pipeline and document rollback procedure
Create privacy-preserving production sample sanitizer and add to ingestion pipeline
